events.title: R1 after investigating: confirms wait

proposal.rationale: The root blocker (pid 371829) has been idle in transaction for only 4.1s (DB-1). The protected_settlement workload is not replayable and has a never_interrupt policy (BIZ-2), so terminating risks double charges or lost settlements. The trade‑off analysis (BIZ-5) shows expected remaining runtime ~41s, costing ~$8,932 in checkout revenue, which fits within the 60s degradation the business tolerates (BIZ-1, BIZ-4). Checkout telemetry (TEL-1) shows 92% success over 15s with 4 timeouts, indicating the system can sustain short‑term degradation. Therefore, waiting allows the blocker to complete naturally within the tolerated window without interrupting the settlement.
proposal.expected_effect: The blocker's transaction will complete after ~41s, releasing its locks. The 12 waiting checkout sessions will gradually recover, bringing checkout success back within the SLO. No locks will be held beyond the 60s business‑tolerated degradation window. The protected settlement continues uninterrupted, avoiding risk of double charges or lost settlements.
proposal.risk_assessment: If the blocker runs longer than the estimated 41s (e.g., >60s), checkout degradation could exceed the business‑tolerated 60s window, potentially breaching the SLO. The primary risk of terminating the settlement (not chosen) is double charges or lost settlements per BIZ-2. Waiting carries minimal risk given the trade‑off fits the tolerance window.
